utterances.text: There is a certain detail that I should like to clarify with you. It says that your work relationship was terminated by consensus, in one of these paragraphs.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV KVOCKA [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Let me find it, please. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SIMIC
utterances.text: Was it by agreement? And why did you ask to be relieved from your duties in the police?

utterances.speaker: MR. SIMIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Paragraph 7, Your Honours, I'm referring to.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV KVOCKA [RESUMED]
utterances.text: It says here that on the 1st of November, 1996, my employment was terminated by mutual agreement.

utterances.speaker: MR. SIMIC
utterances.text: Tell Their Honours; it is your duty to tell the truth, tell them freely why you did this.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV KVOCKA [RESUMED]
utterances.text: I stopped working on this date in the police in Prijedor because an order had arrived from my commander, who informed me that I could no longer work in the police.

utterances.speaker: MR. SIMIC
utterances.text: Why?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV KVOCKA [RESUMED]
utterances.text: The explanation he gave me was that international police forces stationed in Prijedor would not allow me to continue working in the internal affairs bodies, that is, in the police.

utterances.speaker: MR. SIMIC
utterances.text: Was this linked to the public announcement of the indictment of this Honourable Tribunal?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV KVOCKA [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Yes, that was the reason, because the indictment had already been made public.

utterances.speaker: MR. SIMIC
utterances.text: And you yourself submitted a request to terminate your employment.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV KVOCKA [RESUMED]
utterances.text: That was on the advice of my superior.

utterances.speaker: MR. SIMIC
utterances.text: Did you find this hard to do, since you spent your whole career in the police force and that you were considered one of the best policemen in Prijedor municipality?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV KVOCKA [RESUMED]
utterances.text: It was very hard for me. I was very sad not to be able to spend a few more years in the police and to end my career in the police force normally.

utterances.speaker: MR. SIMIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I should now like to ask the usher to help me tender DP8, which we shall comment upon very briefly.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Defence Exhibit D13/1; D13/1A for the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. SIMIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SIMIC
utterances.text: Mr. Kvocka, you have before you a letter addressed by your public security station, where you had spent virtually your entire working lifetime, though it changed its name occasionally. In a sense, they are responding to some questions that we had for them, and I should like to draw your attention to point 3, paragraph 1 of this letter. Were you ever, in this period under review, appointed -- or could you have been appointed to any position of authority, of a superior? I am talking about June 1992.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV KVOCKA [RESUMED]
utterances.text: No, I was never appointed or named to take any kind of leadership role or superior position.

utterances.speaker: MR. SIMIC
utterances.text: Was there any legal possibility for anyone to appoint you to such a position in the Prijedor police station?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV KVOCKA [RESUMED]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SIMIC
utterances.text: Does that mean that in 1992, you performed the duties of patrol sector leader?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV KVOCKA [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SIMIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I only have one more segment to cover regarding the activities of my client. Perhaps this would be an appropriate moment for a break, because, after all, this does require a great deal of concentration. We will be through with this area very quickly. We will be discussing his obligations as a military conscript, in view of his status as a policeman.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. Simic, your suggestion seems to me quite appropriate, reasonable, and sensible. So we are going to have a break. I see in my notes that we should have a 20-minute break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You may be seated. Mr. Simic, you may continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. SIMIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SIMIC
utterances.text: Mr. Kvocka, when you finished your secondary police academy, were you obliged to go and serve your national duty, which was an obligation for all men of age?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV KVOCKA [RESUMED]
utterances.text: No, I did not go.

utterances.speaker: MR. SIMIC
utterances.text: Why?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV KVOCKA [RESUMED]
utterances.text: I was under no obligation to do so, because the law on the military duty provided that the cadets of the secondary police academy were not obliged to serve national duty.

utterances.speaker: MR. SIMIC
utterances.text: Were you still under obligation, according to the laws, the federal and the republican laws, to comply with the military service?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV KVOCKA [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SIMIC
utterances.text: What were your obligations?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV KVOCKA [RESUMED]
utterances.text: My duty consisted in reporting to the Ministry for Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. SIMIC
utterances.text: Did the Ministry have its offices from the federal to the municipal levels?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV KVOCKA [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SIMIC
utterances.text: So did your duty consist in your reporting to the municipal office?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV KVOCKA [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SIMIC
utterances.text: Did you do so?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV KVOCKA [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SIMIC
utterances.text: Did you receive the wartime assignment?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV KVOCKA [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SIMIC
utterances.text: Were you told what was your assignment at that time?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV KVOCKA [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Yes, I was told that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SIMIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us then what that assignment was so that we all know?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV KVOCKA [RESUMED]
utterances.text: My wartime assignment was a military policeman.

utterances.speaker: MR. SIMIC
utterances.text: Were you assigned to a particular unit? Because every military conscript, regardless of his duty, also is assigned a unit where he is to report.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV KVOCKA [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Yes. That was to be the police station or precinct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SIMIC
utterances.text: Were you told what your VES was? VES was the code for your speciality?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV KVOCKA [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SIMIC
utterances.text: Do you recall what it was?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV KVOCKA [RESUMED]
utterances.text: 11107 is what I think the code number is.

utterances.speaker: MR. SIMIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I do not have the originals here. The documents had been submitted to the Tribunal. I'm going to give the explanation, but it's -- our marking is DP12.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Exhibit D14/1.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Excuse me, Mr. Simic, for interrupting you. Mr. Registrar, the previous one -- previous exhibit was D11. Am I mistaken? You said that this exhibit was D14.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President. The previous Exhibit was D13/1.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Thank you. I beg your pardon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SIMIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SIMIC
utterances.text: Mr. Kvocka, you see a letter before you which the Ministry of Defence of Republika Srpska, the Prijedor department, sent to the government of the Republika Srpska, and the government of the Republika Srpska requested this information on behalf of the Tribunal. As item 2, you see the name "Miroslav Kvocka." Is this correct information, that your wartime code is 9121 in Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV KVOCKA [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SIMIC
utterances.text: And is it correct that this number --

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV KVOCKA [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Actually, the number is not correct, because one digit is missing.

utterances.speaker: MR. SIMIC
utterances.text: It should be 11107.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV KVOCKA [RESUMED]
utterances.text: That is correct. It should be 11107. One digit is missing.

utterances.speaker: MR. SIMIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that you were a military policeman? That was to be your wartime duty?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV KVOCKA [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SIMIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Kvocka.

utterances.speaker: MR. SIMIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to tender Exhibit number 53, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Defence Exhibit D15/1; D15/1A for the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. SIMIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SIMIC
utterances.text: Mr. Kvocka, you see a document which is a certificate by the Ministry of Defence, the personnel department, which gives us an interpretation of the code VES 11107, which is defined as a reserve member of the military police, and the rank is "private." The VES code does not comprise any meaning of a rank of officer or superior in other countries; it marks only a regular private soldier?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV KVOCKA [RESUMED]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SIMIC
utterances.text: Does that correspond to what you knew at the time and what you were told when you were tasked with military duty as a conscript?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV KVOCKA [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct. And it is signed by the assistant minister.

utterances.speaker: MR. SIMIC
utterances.text: Very well, Mr. Kvocka. The war in the territory of Bosnia-Herzegovina unfortunately lasted for a very long time and produced the consequences that we have all suffered through. Throughout this war, as a member or -- how shall I put it? -- as a military conscript, were you under obligation to carry out your duties relating to your wartime assignment?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV KVOCKA [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Yes. I was under obligation to comply with it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SIMIC
utterances.text: Throughout the conflict, from its beginning to the end, were you always a member of the police code number VES 11107?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV KVOCKA [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SIMIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would now like to tender 959, and I have the original.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Defence Exhibit D16/1; D16/1A for the English version.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Simic, please excuse me. What is the number that you attach to this document?

utterances.speaker: MR. SIMIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 959.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SIMIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SIMIC
utterances.text: Mr. Kvocka, you have an official certificate issued, in similar cases, by the Ministry for various purposes. Here it states that you -- that in 1992, you were an active-duty police officer in the Prijedor Public Security Station. Did you have any other status other than is mentioned in this document?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV KVOCKA [RESUMED]
utterances.text: What is stated in this document is correct. You said -- you mentioned 1990?

utterances.speaker: MR. SIMIC
utterances.text: No. I mentioned 1992. This is the only year I'm referring to.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV KVOCKA [RESUMED]
utterances.text: In 1992 I was an active-duty police officer, as it is stated here.

utterances.speaker: MR. SIMIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Let us sum up this. So according to the military assignments and military duties, in 1992 you had no other status than that of a military policeman, that is, a policeman in your official station?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV KVOCKA [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SIMIC
utterances.text: Before we move on to the central area of our questioning, you just mentioned that it was very hard for you to leave the job which you were very attached to?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV KVOCKA [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Yes, and I still have difficulties in coming to terms with it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SIMIC
utterances.text: The news of your arrest, did it produce an incident in the Sanski Most area? I just want to touch on it and then move on.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV KVOCKA [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Several days after my arrest, I received information that in Sanski Most my wife's brother was also arrested by the local police there and detained for some 20 hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. SIMIC
utterances.text: What is your wife's brother's name?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV KVOCKA [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Rizak Crnalic, called Rica.

utterances.speaker: MR. SIMIC
utterances.text: What was stated as the reason for his arrest by the police in the Bihac-Sanski Most canton, that is, the local police in Sanski Most?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV KVOCKA [RESUMED]
utterances.text: He explained to my wife later on, after he saw her, that on that evening he had consumed some alcohol, that he went around Sanski Most cursing President Izetbegovic, and that he was then detained by the police there.

utterances.speaker: MR. SIMIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SIMIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now, Your Honours, I want to move on to the events that we're all most interested in, and I'll proceed without further ado.

utterances.speaker: MR. SIMIC
utterances.text: Mr. Kvocka, when did you first have contact with the detention centre in Omarska?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV KVOCKA [RESUMED]
utterances.text: In the night of 28/29 or perhaps the night before. I am unable to clear it up in my mind. I was duty officer in the precinct in Omarska.

utterances.speaker: MR. SIMIC
utterances.text: Where were you on duty?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV KVOCKA [RESUMED]
utterances.text: I was inside the building, in the facility itself, in the duty room.

utterances.speaker: MR. SIMIC
utterances.text: Did you have any communication means as any other policeman?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV KVOCKA [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Yes, a radio transmitter.

utterances.speaker: MR. SIMIC
utterances.text: Were there any other police officers who were also on duty with you?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV KVOCKA [RESUMED]
utterances.text: There were two additional reserve officers with me.

utterances.speaker: MR. SIMIC
utterances.text: Can you recall their names?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV KVOCKA [RESUMED]
utterances.text: No, not at the moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. SIMIC
utterances.text: Were there any patrols who had come back from patrols as one of the ways in which police duties were conducted that night?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV KVOCKA [RESUMED]
utterances.text: I believe that the patrols which had been out in the field had already come back that night, and some of them may have only come back in the morning, but they were out in the field.

utterances.speaker: MR. SIMIC
utterances.text: What happened between 28th and 29th, or perhaps 27th and 28th?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV KVOCKA [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Sometime around 0200 --

utterances.speaker: MR. SIMIC
utterances.text: This was the month of May, 1992. Can we go on?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV KVOCKA [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SIMIC
utterances.text: Can you please repeat the exact date and month so that we can resolve any lingering dilemmas?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV KVOCKA [RESUMED]
utterances.text: That was either the night of the 28th/29th or the night before, that is, of May 1992. This was when I was the officer on duty in the police precinct in Omarska, with two reserve police officers. Somewhere between 0200 and 0300 we received notice through the radio.

utterances.speaker: MR. SIMIC
utterances.text: Who called you?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV KVOCKA [RESUMED]
utterances.text: It was Dusan Jankovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. SIMIC
utterances.text: Could we repeat who Dusan Jankovic was?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV KVOCKA [RESUMED]
utterances.text: At that time he was the chief for the police.

utterances.speaker: MR. SIMIC
utterances.text: And what did he say?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV KVOCKA [RESUMED]
utterances.text: He told me to immediately come to him, and he told me that he was in the area of Omarska mining complex.

utterances.speaker: MR. SIMIC
utterances.text: Did he ask for the commander beforehand?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV KVOCKA [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Yes. He asked whether the commander was there, by chance.

utterances.speaker: MR. SIMIC
utterances.text: And what did you say?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV KVOCKA [RESUMED]
utterances.text: I said that he was not. The commander stayed on the premises very seldom.

utterances.speaker: MR. SIMIC
utterances.text: You said that this was radioed in.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV KVOCKA [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SIMIC
utterances.text: What did you do after receiving this request?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV KVOCKA [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Given this order, I got into my vehicle and I went to where he said he was.

utterances.speaker: MR. SIMIC
utterances.text: You knew where the Omarska complex was.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV KVOCKA [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, I knew about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SIMIC
utterances.text: When you arrived there, what did you find?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV KVOCKA [RESUMED]
utterances.text: When I passed through the gate, through the main gate, it was dark, as I said, and I found Dusan Jankovic and Milutin Cadjo, who were sitting in an official vehicle in front of the main administration building of the mining complex.

utterances.speaker: MR. SIMIC
utterances.text: Did they address you?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV KVOCKA [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Yes, they did. I told him that I was coming in response to his order. MR. SIMIC [Interpretation] In order for us to be able to follow everything better, I'm going to interrupt this line of questioning, and I would like Mr. Kvocka to describe for us the layout of this facility to where he came so that we can all be better oriented about who was where. With your permission, Your Honours. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SIMIC
utterances.text: So, Mr. Kvocka, you arrived on the premises of the compound, of the mining complex. You passed through the main gate.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV KVOCKA [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SIMIC
utterances.text: And where is the main gate?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV KVOCKA [RESUMED]
utterances.text: It is about 1.5 kilometres from the main administration building.

utterances.speaker: MR. SIMIC
utterances.text: Is there any kind of reception area at the front gate?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV KVOCKA [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SIMIC
utterances.text: When you arrived there, was there any security there?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV KVOCKA [RESUMED]
utterances.text: There was one guard, which was a security guard employed by the company.

utterances.speaker: MR. SIMIC
utterances.text: So there were no police officers there.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV KVOCKA [RESUMED]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SIMIC
utterances.text: And now you entered the Omarska complex. The model in front of you, does it reflect accurately what you remember? The front entrance is close to Ms. Hollis, if she will excuse me.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV KVOCKA [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Yes. This model reflects what the complex looked like, that is, what the buildings in the complex were.

utterances.speaker: MR. SIMIC
utterances.text: So the first building that is closest to the Prosecution team, what is it called?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV KVOCKA [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Yes. That is the administration building, and that is the low-rise building.

utterances.speaker: MR. SIMIC
utterances.text: Is there a restaurant that was part of this administration building?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV KVOCKA [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SIMIC
utterances.text: Is it towards the small White House?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV KVOCKA [RESUMED]
utterances.text: I cannot see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SIMIC
utterances.text: Could you please rise and see if you can see it from there.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV KVOCKA [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see it now. I see the area of the restaurant. That would be the lower portion of that building.

utterances.speaker: MR. SIMIC
utterances.text: Well, perhaps you can actually show us so that we can all better understand.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV KVOCKA [RESUMED]
utterances.text: This here [indicates] was referred to as the administrative building of the complex.

utterances.speaker: MR. SIMIC
utterances.text: And there's a restaurant within its composition.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV KVOCKA [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Yes. There's a slightly separated facility, which was the restaurant, the canteen.

utterances.speaker: MR. SIMIC
utterances.text: Are the walls of the building glass partitions?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV KVOCKA [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Yes. Along here [indicates].

utterances.speaker: MR. SIMIC
utterances.text: In the front of the building, were there any garages?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV KVOCKA [RESUMED]
utterances.text: In the front, you mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. SIMIC
utterances.text: In front of you, I mean.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV KVOCKA [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Yes. Here [indicates], there was a small garage here.

utterances.speaker: MR. SIMIC
utterances.text: And the lower part of the ground floor?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV KVOCKA [RESUMED]
utterances.text: In the lower part of the administrative building, I'm not quite sure; I don't know what its purpose was.

utterances.speaker: MR. SIMIC
utterances.text: While the investigating centre was there, was it in operation?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV KVOCKA [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SIMIC
utterances.text: On the floor above the garage, and the area that you do not know what purpose it served, what is there?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV KVOCKA [RESUMED]
utterances.text: On the storey above, there was a series of offices.

utterances.speaker: MR. SIMIC
utterances.text: Were they on the left- and right-hand side?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV KVOCKA [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Yes. There's a corridor along here, and on both sides of the corridor were the offices.

utterances.speaker: MR. SIMIC
utterances.text: Were these offices where the interviews took place?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV KVOCKA [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SIMIC
utterances.text: Let us now move on to the pista. What was that area in the Omarska complex? Where was it?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV KVOCKA [RESUMED]
utterances.text: We used the term "pista" for the area in between this large building and the administration building.

utterances.speaker: MR. SIMIC
utterances.text: Was it a concrete floor?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV KVOCKA [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Yes, all this was actually asphalt.

utterances.speaker: MR. SIMIC
utterances.text: Now let us look at the big building. What was that within the complex?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV KVOCKA [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Could I just add one thing, please. At that time, there were sort of concrete vases or planters which were located here [indicates], so the pista was delineated in that way.

utterances.speaker: MR. SIMIC
utterances.text: While it was the investigating centre, were they there all the time?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV KVOCKA [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Yes, they were.

utterances.speaker: MR. SIMIC
utterances.text: Let us now move on to this big building. What was that in the overall complex of Omarska?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV KVOCKA [RESUMED]
utterances.text: While the mine was operational, these were workshops, as far as I know, and garages for the heavy-duty vehicles.

utterances.speaker: MR. SIMIC
utterances.text: That building, did it have a storey?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV KVOCKA [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Yes, it did.

utterances.speaker: MR. SIMIC
utterances.text: What was on the upper storey?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV KVOCKA [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Well, there were several premises, but I didn't go in there. There were two or three different ones.

utterances.speaker: MR. SIMIC
utterances.text: The small house, painted white, and it is referred to as the White House, was it always there?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV KVOCKA [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. SIMIC
utterances.text: So this corresponds to where it was. How big was that White House?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV KVOCKA [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Well, looking at it on this scale, it was much smaller compared to the other buildings. I don't know the exact dimensions.

utterances.speaker: MR. SIMIC
utterances.text: Was it painted white?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV KVOCKA [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. SIMIC
utterances.text: What about this building over here, which is on par with the white building? What was that?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV KVOCKA [RESUMED]
utterances.text: That facility is one that I noticed as being there, but I never went into it and I don't know what purpose it served.

utterances.speaker: MR. SIMIC
utterances.text: You do not know what purpose it served.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV KVOCKA [RESUMED]
utterances.text: No, I do not. Even when the mining complex was operational, I don't know what purpose it served.

utterances.speaker: MR. SIMIC
utterances.text: There was another little building or facility with a flat roof. This end.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV KVOCKA [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Are you thinking of this one here [indicates]?

utterances.speaker: MR. SIMIC
utterances.text: Yes, I am.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV KVOCKA [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Yes, I did notice that facility, but once again, I cannot say what it was used for. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. SIMIC
utterances.text: As a policeman, in performing your regular duties, did you go into this Omarska complex previously?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV KVOCKA [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Yes, I did, on several occasions.

utterances.speaker: MR. SIMIC
utterances.text: This layout corresponds to the existing situation on the ground, does it not?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV KVOCKA [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SIMIC
utterances.text: So we will be able to adapt some of the details you have given to questions relating to that general area, complex, and compound.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV KVOCKA [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Yes, you will.

utterances.speaker: MR. SIMIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you report to the commander Cadjo and Jankovic when you arrived?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV KVOCKA [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. SIMIC
utterances.text: What did they tell you?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV KVOCKA [RESUMED]
utterances.text: The chief of police, Dule Jankovic, told me that I was to go back to the police department, or precinct, and that I should try and find Zeljko Meakic; that I should tell him, convey to him, that according to a schedule and plan of some kind for raising the reserve police force, that he should do this, activate the reserve police force, which was, at the time, not in the department or precinct. And afterwards, that these men should be brought to the compound, to the mining compound, and that there would be a man there to receive him and to explain to him what he was supposed to do next.

utterances.speaker: MR. SIMIC
utterances.text: Did you receive any kind of information as to the nature of the assignment on that particular evening?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV KVOCKA [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Then? No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. SIMIC
utterances.text: So you returned to the precinct, and what did you do then?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV KVOCKA [RESUMED]
utterances.text: When I returned to the precinct, as there was a list of couriers in the precinct and the assignments of the duty officer, I was to see that the assignments were carried out by those couriers to round up the people, to collect the people that Jankovic had mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MR. SIMIC
utterances.text: Let's make a slight digression here, Mr. Kvocka, if we may. You said a moment ago, you said that "Mr. Jankovic told me," that was the sentence that you used, that Mr. Meakic, according to a plan on raising the -- calling up the reserve policemen, that he should act. Now, when he used this word "plan," did you think he meant a plan with regard to the functioning of Omarska, or the plan of work to call up the reserve police force?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV KVOCKA [RESUMED]
utterances.text: It was my impression that he meant that we should proceed according to the general plan to call up the reserve police force, the policemen who were at home, to call them up, and nothing else.

utterances.speaker: MR. SIMIC
utterances.text: So you did not gain the impression that he actually meant a plan which was in any way linked to that particular situation, but that it was a general situation.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV KVOCKA [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SIMIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Were you able to send the courier on his way to collect and inform the people, the reservists?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV KVOCKA [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SIMIC
utterances.text: Did they begin to gather?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV KVOCKA [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SIMIC
utterances.text: What was the time? When did they begin to gather?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV KVOCKA [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Well, people began to gather at around 6.00, 6.30, 7.00 p.m.

utterances.speaker: MR. SIMIC
utterances.text: Were you able to contact Mr. Meakic, in view of the telephone communications and all the rest?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV KVOCKA [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Well, sometime around 7.00, he himself turned up.

utterances.speaker: MR. SIMIC
utterances.text: Did you take these policemen off to the business complex of Omarska?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV KVOCKA [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Yes, we did go there, and in several tours, because we had a transportation problem.

utterances.speaker: MR. SIMIC
utterances.text: When you arrived, what did the police do?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV KVOCKA [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Which do you mean? You mean the police force that had just arrived?

utterances.speaker: MR. SIMIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV KVOCKA [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Well, there was a man there, or perhaps two men who received us there, and they told us that we would be replacing them. One of these people who met us took over the people who had arrived and deployed them, distributed them, around these facilities, these buildings here [indicates].

utterances.speaker: MR. SIMIC
utterances.text: Does that mean that there were already some people there, and did you see those people when you had contact with Mr. Jankovic? Was there something extraordinary, out of the ordinary? Were there buses there, or was it just a compound as we can see it in front of us?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV KVOCKA [RESUMED]
utterances.text: When I arrived by invitation from Jankovic, his vehicle, and I could have shown this a moment ago, his vehicle was at the entrance to the administration building. It was night-time, but several buses could be seen. Perhaps there were ten buses in all, and they were parked in two rows. The first two or three buses which I saw -- actually, they were the first two or three buses in the rear, the ones that I was able to see, were empty, but there were buses which were full. There were people in the buses.

utterances.speaker: MR. SIMIC
utterances.text: Did you notice any people outside the buses, that they were being taken off somewhere, or anything like that?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV KVOCKA [RESUMED]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SIMIC
utterances.text: When you returned and when you were met by the police representatives, do you know who they were?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV KVOCKA [RESUMED]
utterances.text: At that time, we didn't know who they were, no. All we saw was that they were uniformed and had the same uniforms as us, that they wore police uniforms as well. But the man who met us had a slightly different uniform than the one that we wore in Omarska.

utterances.speaker: MR. SIMIC
utterances.text: So judging by their uniforms, they were policemen, were they not?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV KVOCKA [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Yes, because later on, all policemen were required to wear uniforms of that kind, in the months to come.

utterances.speaker: MR. SIMIC
utterances.text: So he was a forerunner to this new uniform; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV KVOCKA [RESUMED]
utterances.text: It would appear that way, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SIMIC
utterances.text: Were these people from the police station at Omarska, the public security station there -- in view of the fact that some 150 people worked there and you probably knew all of them -- were they people you knew?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV KVOCKA [RESUMED]
utterances.text: No. I did not know a single man who was standing there.

utterances.speaker: MR. SIMIC
utterances.text: Did they introduce themselves, show any ID cards, or anything of that kind?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV KVOCKA [RESUMED]
utterances.text: The man wearing the uniform that I spoke about a moment ago, who met us, said that they were policemen from Banja Luka and that they would be leaving on holiday, to have a brief holiday, and that we would be taking up their duties.

utterances.speaker: MR. SIMIC
utterances.text: What duties were those?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV KVOCKA [RESUMED]
utterances.text: It was the duty of providing security for the facility, physical security, as we refer to it in the police.

utterances.speaker: MR. SIMIC
utterances.text: Now, this group of policemen, the ones that you came across when you got there, did they take up the people from the Omarska police station and position them anywhere?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV KVOCKA [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Yes. That man, and the other man standing there with him who greeted us and met us, they positioned people around the facility.

utterances.speaker: MR. SIMIC
utterances.text: Were there any buses there then?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV KVOCKA [RESUMED]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SIMIC
utterances.text: So they had left during that interval.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV KVOCKA [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Yes, quite probably they had left.

utterances.speaker: MR. SIMIC
utterances.text: Was Mr. Jankovic and Mr. Cadjo there?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV KVOCKA [RESUMED]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SIMIC
utterances.text: They had left too?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV KVOCKA [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SIMIC
utterances.text: Did you now see any people? And we're talking about 6.00 or 7.00 in the morning. Did you see any people?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV KVOCKA [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Yes. You could make out people from the positions that we were standing, externally to the compound.

utterances.speaker: MR. SIMIC
utterances.text: Where were the people?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV KVOCKA [RESUMED]
utterances.text: You could see people that morning only through a small door here [indicates], which exists here on the ground floor of the administrative building.

utterances.speaker: MR. SIMIC
utterances.text: You mean the garage?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV KVOCKA [RESUMED]
utterances.text: No, not the garage; another door in the centre of the building.

utterances.speaker: MR. SIMIC
utterances.text: Did you see people in other parts, in the other buildings?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV KVOCKA [RESUMED]
utterances.text: No. You couldn't see any people in any of the other buildings.

utterances.speaker: MR. SIMIC
utterances.text: When Mr. Meakic learnt about the new task and situation, did he give the impression that he was surprised or that he expected something like that to happen?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV KVOCKA [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Meakic was surprised, in my view, and he sort of spoke out loud and thought out loud, said he didn't know what was going on. He was confused. He just knew that there was this assignment that we were taking over from the Banja Luka police, to put it in those terms, and he stood around there for some time with us.

utterances.speaker: MR. SIMIC
utterances.text: Did he say that he would try, in view of the potential that the police station had and the Omarska department, that he would try and avoid the assignment?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV KVOCKA [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Well, he did speak about that, yes. He said that the best thing would be for us not to undertake the assignment because we didn't have the resources required.

utterances.speaker: MR. SIMIC
utterances.text: In the course of that day, did he go to seek out some additional information and try and solve the problem in any way and his activities as commander?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV KVOCKA [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Yes. He went on straight away after some 40 minutes or one hour. He went off straight away.

utterances.speaker: MR. SIMIC
utterances.text: Do you know where he went?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV KVOCKA [RESUMED]
utterances.text: I don't know exactly. I don't know who he went to report to.

utterances.speaker: MR. SIMIC
utterances.text: When he returned, did he give you a report of any kind? Did he give you any information? Did he issue any orders? Did he tell you anything?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV KVOCKA [RESUMED]
utterances.text: No, nothing special. He didn't inform us of anything special, but he just reiterated the assignment that we had already been given by the Banja Luka men, and he said that we had received orders to provide for the physical security of the facilities in which the detainees were located. He said that he was told that this would go on for some 15 days, and that he would see what he could do to make this period shorter.

utterances.speaker: MR. SIMIC
utterances.text: Did he mention who the detainees were?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV KVOCKA [RESUMED]
utterances.text: He didn't explain any of this to us at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. SIMIC
utterances.text: The people were detained. Did he mention how the food supply would be organised? There are a lot a problems to be solved in a large compound of this kind.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV KVOCKA [RESUMED]
utterances.text: No. He made no mention of that. He didn't speak to us policemen about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SIMIC
utterances.text: Now, the first shift of people who had arrived in the locality of the Omarska compound, how many arrived? How many policemen arrived?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV KVOCKA [RESUMED]
utterances.text: About 20.

utterances.speaker: MR. SIMIC
utterances.text: Let us repeat once again. Was there any type of hierarchy? Was there a commander, leader, or the policemen and reserve policemen which were equal in status?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV KVOCKA [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Well, it was the same, just as it was in the police precinct of Omarska.

utterances.speaker: MR. SIMIC
utterances.text: In this interval with the takeover of power, were there any changes made?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV KVOCKA [RESUMED]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SIMIC
utterances.text: What did you do, in concrete terms, in the first days of your assignment? What did Mr. Meakic -- what tasks did he assign to you?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV KVOCKA [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Well, on that first day he told me personally that I would be the duty officer, and the other policemen had already taken up their positions. They had already been on duty since the morning, where they had been positioned by the Banja Luka policemen or their commander, most probably, and that was how the day was to evolve until a new schedule had been drawn up.

utterances.speaker: MR. SIMIC
utterances.text: Were you given any additional assignments to assist, in any way, the reserve policemen who were there then, who were in the majority at the time?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV KVOCKA [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Well, in concrete terms, he told me. I think I was the only one. Perhaps Branislav Bojic was another one. I think he was there too. So he said I would be the duty officer for that day, and I should be around if needed and if the reserve policemen had any questions to ask from the daily routine of policing, if they had any problems or anything like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SIMIC
utterances.text: Did Borislav Bojic get any instructions of that kind? He was also an active and experienced policeman and was a candidate, together with Mr. Meakic?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV KVOCKA [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Well, his instructions referred to all active policemen, in principle for other tasks and assignments as well, but in this particular case he addressed us.

utterances.speaker: MR. SIMIC
utterances.text: So is it standard that an active policeman, in effecting his duties, should be at the service, so to speak, of reserve policemen, to help them in any way?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV KVOCKA [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Yes, at all times and in all kinds of police work. An active policeman is always there to train and educate the reserve policemen.

utterances.speaker: MR. SIMIC
utterances.text: Mr. Kvocka, would you try and remember some of the names of the policemen who arrived at the Omarska compound on that first day? You mentioned Branislav Bojic. Can you remember any other names?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV KVOCKA [RESUMED]
utterances.text: You mean the active policemen?

utterances.speaker: MR. SIMIC
utterances.text: Well, both, active and reserve.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV KVOCKA [RESUMED]
utterances.text: It's difficult for me to recall their names at this point. I know most of the reserve policemen who worked at some given point, but on that particular morning, who was there, which of the reserve policemen was there, I just can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. SIMIC
utterances.text: Well, we'll go back to the question of those policemen later on. But tell us, in concrete terms, what your duties were that day. What did you do?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV KVOCKA [RESUMED]
utterances.text: I spent the day in front of the entrance mostly, in front of the entrance to the administrative building mostly, on the pista, but nearer, closer to the administrative building.

utterances.speaker: MR. SIMIC
utterances.text: Did you have any contacts with the guards that day?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV KVOCKA [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SIMIC
utterances.text: Were there any questions of the following type: "What are we doing here? How long are we going to be here?"

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV KVOCKA [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Yes. All of them would ask me questions of that kind or make comments. They were thinking out loud about this situation in general.

utterances.speaker: MR. SIMIC
utterances.text: Mr. Kvocka, before you arrived in Omarska, did you have any information whatsoever that in a time in the future you would have any tasks or assignments of this kind?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV KVOCKA [RESUMED]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SIMIC
utterances.text: Did you hear that an investigating centre was being established or was this your first encounter with the centre?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV KVOCKA [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Well, no, there was no talk about any of this before that. The first information I received was when I got there that morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. SIMIC
utterances.text: Mr. Kvocka, when the buses were there and then when the buses had left, did you notice anything out of the ordinary opposite the restaurant? Were there any bodies there, corpses, the bodies of dead people, anything of that kind?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV KVOCKA [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Well, after 8.00 or 9.00 a.m., it was daylight, and while I was in front of the administrative building, as I've already said, in the pista region, on the same height, on that yellow surface --

utterances.speaker: MR. SIMIC
utterances.text: Could you get up, please, and show us, because this is an important point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Perhaps you could give Mr. Kvocka the pointer and help him, and give him the headphones with the long cord.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV KVOCKA [RESUMED]
utterances.text: While I was in this area here [indicates], as I said, when it was daylight, at 8.00 or 9.00 a.m., in this area, on the green surface, there were three or four dead bodies laying there. These bodies were lying on the grass, but you could see that they were dead.

utterances.speaker: MR. SIMIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SIMIC
utterances.text: Were they males? Could you tell?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV KVOCKA [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Yes, they were. They were men.

utterances.speaker: MR. SIMIC
utterances.text: Did you hear later on how it came about that there were three or four bodies there? Because you will agree with me this isn't a customary thing to see.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV KVOCKA [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Later on, when the guards could talk to each other a little bit, then it was said that the previous guards had told them, when they were taking over their shifts, that they were bodies of people who had tried to escape during the night. Yes. They were people who had tried to escape during the night, and that they intervened by shooting them.

utterances.speaker: MR. SIMIC
utterances.text: Does that mean that those people had been killed when they were being brought into custody in the Omarska compound?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV KVOCKA [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SIMIC
utterances.text: Did this occur before the members of the Omarska police precinct had taken up their duties?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV KVOCKA [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SIMIC
utterances.text: Did you hear where this happened? Was this something that was talked about in the compound?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV KVOCKA [RESUMED]
utterances.text: As I have already said, the guards who replaced the previous guards on duty said that when they left the buses, that they tried to escape, and that that is the spot where they were shot and that that is the spot where they now lay.

utterances.speaker: MR. SIMIC
utterances.text: Were there any other traces in the area that that could have happened in some other place? Were there any traces of blood or any other objects which would lead you to conclude that the killing had not taken place on that spot but elsewhere?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV KVOCKA [RESUMED]
utterances.text: No. There was nothing to indicate that the killings had taken place in another area.

utterances.speaker: MR. SIMIC
utterances.text: Were there any traces of the asphalt having been cleaned, washed?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV KVOCKA [RESUMED]
utterances.text: No. Everything was quite in order.

utterances.speaker: MR. SIMIC
utterances.text: Mr. Kvocka, did Mr. Meakic see that or was he informed about what had happened?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV KVOCKA [RESUMED]
utterances.text: He saw it at the same time as I did, perhaps five or six minutes or ten minutes before me, but we saw it almost at the same time.

utterances.speaker: MR. SIMIC
utterances.text: Did Mr. Meakic order any investigations into the event?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV KVOCKA [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Well, he didn't tell us anything along those lines.

utterances.speaker: MR. SIMIC
utterances.text: And the police precinct, in general terms, would it be obliged to start up investigations into criminal acts in general, or would somebody else do that?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV KVOCKA [RESUMED]
utterances.text: No. In our description of our jobs, we would have to ensure and set up a -- protect those bodies, that they should not be touched, and then the criminal crime department should be informed and further steps taken.

utterances.speaker: MR. SIMIC
utterances.text: Do you know if Mr. Meakic did that?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV KVOCKA [RESUMED]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. SIMIC
utterances.text: Thank you. We're a little tired already. How long did those bodies lie there?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV KVOCKA [RESUMED]
utterances.text: They had been lying there for at least two -- they lay there for at least two days.

utterances.speaker: MR. SIMIC
utterances.text: And nobody undertook any steps?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV KVOCKA [RESUMED]
utterances.text: No, they didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. SIMIC
utterances.text: When were the bodies taken off?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV KVOCKA [RESUMED]
utterances.text: After those two days, the bodies were, quite simply, taken away.

utterances.speaker: MR. SIMIC
utterances.text: Did you see them being taken away, transported, or did you just see that they were no longer there?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV KVOCKA [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Well, one day a small truck arrived, a van, and two men, together with the driver, and they loaded up the bodies and they were taken away.

utterances.speaker: MR. SIMIC
utterances.text: Those two men that you mentioned that came with the small truck, did they belong to the Omarska police station department?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV KVOCKA [RESUMED]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SIMIC
utterances.text: You didn't know them?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV KVOCKA [RESUMED]
utterances.text: No. No. They were not in uniform at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. SIMIC
utterances.text: Did they appear later on in Omarska? Did you ever see them again?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV KVOCKA [RESUMED]
utterances.text: I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. SIMIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, it is half past 2.00. Perhaps it is time for us to interrupt, unless you planned for us to make up for the time we lost at the beginning. It is up to you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. Please be seated, Mr. Kvocka. I cannot ask everyone to stay an hour longer, because we have other engagements. So we will adjourn now and we will resume tomorrow. At 9.30 tomorrow we meet again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: at 2.33 p.m., to be reconvened on Thursday, the 2nd day of March, 2000, at 9.30 a.m.
